subject: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment — onboarding checklist and legal backfill
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@helixanalytics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial metering / entitlement questions before onboarding

Hi Kimberly / Aditya —

Thanks for the onboarding doc you sent Friday. We took a first pass and flagged three items we'd like clarified before our legal/finance team signs off:

1) Entitlement mapping: Helix sells feature-tier SKUs at account level (bronze/silver/gold). We need a clear mapping from an AWS Marketplace entitlement SKU to our internal tenant_id and feature-tier so we can reconcile billing.

2) Metering payload shape: our engineering team has a serverless adapter that emits event counts. Is there a recommended envelope for the AWS metering API so retries / idempotency can be reconciled on our side?

3) Backfill / grace period: our procurement wants a 2-week backfill window from go-live for initial activation spikes — can Redwood support metering backfill and a reconciliation window?

Attaching the sample payload our system emits. Happy to hop on a short call next week.

—Tom
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Helix Analytics

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-07-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial metering / entitlement questions before onboarding

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top, details below.

1) Entitlement mapping: Redwood will surface the Marketplace entitlement SKU in webhook payloads and in the activation callbacks. We recommend a small mapping table on your side (marketplace_sku -> tenant_id -> feature_tier). We can share a sample mapping script and a one-time import template.

2) Metering payload: Redwood expects an idempotent event_id and an iso timestamp; we also support a usage_amount and optional dimensions for feature tier. See Dev's sample below.

3) Backfill: We can support a 14-day backfill window for the initial go-live if it's requested in advance and included in the SOW. Finance will need a notarized count export for audit.

Open items for Redwood:
- Legal: confirm SOW amendment language for backfill and effective date.
- Infra: confirm webhook signing header algorithm and shared secret rotation window.
- Ops: set up a reconciliation runbook for first 4 weeks (daily for week 1, then weekly).

Propose a short sync on Wed 07/06 — 30 minutes. I'll send a calendar hold once you confirm.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@helixanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-07-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial metering / entitlement questions before onboarding

Adding the infra details Tom asked for and an example webhook / reconciliation approach.

-- recommended meter event envelope (minimal):
{
  "event_id": "uuid-v4",
  "timestamp": "2027-07-03T14:20:00Z",
  "tenant_id": "helix-tenant-123",
  "marketplace_sku": "redwood.saas.gold",
  "usage_amount": 1,
  "dimensions": { "feature": "inference_tokens" }
}

Notes:
- event_id must be unique per usage event and retried with same id when sending again.
- Redwood validates X-Redwood-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256) for webhook callbacks; we recommend the same mechanism for your metering forwards so we can cross-validate.
- For entitlement mapping we can accept either (a) marketplace_sku in the metering payload, or (b) you can pre-seed a mapping table via our CSV uploader (recommended for performance).

Operational plan for go-live (proposed):
- Day 0 (go-live): enable marketplace metering endpoint, set webhook secret, start daily reconcile job.
- Day 1-14: daily reconciliation and manual review of any mismatched tenant_id/sku. Redwood will provide a delta export.
- Day 15+: switch to weekly reconciliation for 6 weeks, then monthly.

Open question for procurement/legal: how should chargebacks for late activation be represented in the SOW? If Helix wants automatic meter backfill we need the SOW to include explicit acceptance criteria and audit procedures.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood

Kimberly / Aditya —

Procurement and Legal reviewed the SOW draft and requested two contract redlines before they're comfortable approving the 14-day backfill: 

1) Audit window: we need audit logs for reconciliation exports preserved for 90 days post-backfill.
2) Liability cap: we want a clause limiting refunds for miscounted metering to the amount invoiced for the affected billing period (standard).

Also can you provide a DocuSign link for the updated SOW? We prefer not to keep unsigned SOWs on email.

Thanks — I'll be on the Wed sync if you confirm time.

Sarah Li
Director, Procurement
Helix Analytics

- Engineering (Helix): confirm whether you will include marketplace_sku in metering payload or if you want Redwood to seed mapping via CSV. If you choose CSV, please provide the file by 2027-07-08. (owner: Tom)
- Infra (Redwood): share webhook secret rotation guide and reconcile runbook by 2027-07-08. (owner: dev_patel)
- Ops (Redwood + Helix): calendar the canary window (07/14 - 07/28) and enable daily exports first two weeks. (owner: monica_patel)
